text:
Chris: hey everyone, new here. quick one: I grabbed a hosted API key to try streaming locally but my terminal keeps getting 429s and the stream stops mid-response. is hosted expected to be throttled for dev laptops? :thinking:
Sam (DevEx): welcome Chris! hosted keys are typically tighter on rate limits and may be subject to org IP rules. for iterative local dev use the sandbox key or a CI token. sandbox supports streaming but with smaller burst capacity.
Tash: also check if you're on a corp VPN that egresses through a different IP. hosted + IP allowlist combos can cause weird rejections on chunked streams.
Chris: cool. how do I swap my app to sandbox? it reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from env currently.
Sam (DevEx): easiest is to export the sandbox token locally. Example for a quick streaming test:
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-sandbox-abc123"
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"hello"}'
```
Chris: is keeping that sandbox token in a .env ok on my laptop?
Sam (DevEx): fine for local dev but never commit. Add .env to .gitignore. Prefer OS keychain or local secret store if you can. For CI use ephemeral CI tokens from the Console (Service tokens -> CI token) so you don't store hosted keys in CI.
Chris: i'm also hitting a sandbox burst limit when running a bunch of tests. how do I request a temporary increase?
Sam (DevEx): file at https://redwood.internal/devex/keys-requests or email devex@redwood.ai with team, repo, expected qps, and window. we can grant short-lived increases for demos.
Tash: dev tip: use batch_size=1 and trim max_tokens for debug streaming to conserve quota. add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s.
infra-bot: Note: if your org has IP whitelisting enabled, hosted keys from unlisted IPs may see rate rejections. To request IP allowlist add, open an infra ticket with your devbox IP.
Chris: awesome, switching to sandbox now. thanks!
